metadata.title: Environmental Awareness in TIMSS 2023: Patterns in Achievement, Attitudes, Behaviors, and Contexts
metadata.venue: Boston College, TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses TIMSS 2023 contextual questionnaire data merged to the student level and applies sampling weights to account for TIMSS’s complex survey design. Specifically, after merging Home, School, and Student questionnaire data to the student unit, the SENWGT weight is applied; for Teacher questionnaire data, the SCIWGT weight is applied. The analyses are conducted with sampling-weighted averages of posterior class probabilities to estimate class prevalence and with sampling-weighted expected achievement by class. The manuscript does not report replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife), but it does state that standard errors follow the TIMSS 2023 technical procedures.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a TIMSS Insights report that summarizes environmental knowledge scale scores and uses MG-LCA to form latent classes from questionnaire items. The excerpted text does not document a specific missing-data strategy for the environmental knowledge scale scores or the questionnaire items used in the MG-LCA, beyond excluding records with fewer than two responses across selected environmental-awareness items. Because the report does not explicitly state how missingness in the achievement/scale estimation stage was handled (e.g., PV-based procedures), the missing-data handling is treated as not reported. This represents a reporting gap for analysts attempting to reproduce the exact estimation pipeline.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report states that all countries and benchmarking participants that administered contextual questionnaires were included. Observations with fewer than two responses across the selected environmental-awareness items were excluded from the MG-LCA analyses (i.e., any record with only a single response to the selected items was removed). To ensure a consistent unit of analysis, Home, Teacher, and School questionnaire data were merged to the student level before analysis. All variables were recoded so that higher response categories reflect stronger agreement or greater frequency. Sampling weights were then applied throughout the analyses to account for the complex survey design.

data.outcome_summary: This TIMSS Insights report uses TIMSS 2023 science assessment data and multiple contextual questionnaires to describe environmental awareness at Grades 4 and 8. Environmental knowledge is measured with science items from biology and earth science domains (e.g., climate change, Earth’s resources, ecosystems), and the report presents country-level average scale scores and gender differences. To characterize patterns in environmental attitudes and self-reported behaviors (and related contextual variables from parents, schools, and teachers), the authors fit multiple-group latent class analyses (MG-LCAs) separately by grade and questionnaire set, constraining item response probabilities to be comparable across countries while allowing class prevalence to vary by country. Sampling weights are applied (SENWGT for student/home/school merged data; SCIWGT for teacher data), and class prevalence is estimated using sampling-weighted averages of posterior class probabilities. The report benchmarks and interprets expected environmental knowledge by latent class membership, while cautioning that socially desirable responding and insufficient effort may distort self-reports.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an IEA TIMSS Insights report rather than an empirical ML prediction paper. It does not train or compare machine-learning predictive models; instead, it uses MG-LCA (a psychometric mixture modeling approach) to profile response patterns and then reports descriptive/benchmarking relationships with environmental knowledge. As a result, fields related to ML techniques, predictive targets, and ML-style performance metrics are intentionally empty, and the extraction focuses on assessment design, weighting, and the latent-class profiling results.
